_comment: P(navigator.maxTouchPoints | gpu_class). One row per GPU class, each row a
weighted pool drawn like every other pool in this package: cumulative, in
order, never reordered and never shortened in place.
EVERY ROW PUTS ALL ITS MASS ON 0, DELIBERATELY. That is a data statement,
not a placeholder: we have no measured joint distribution of touch-point
counts against GPU class on Windows, and the 474 renderers in the pool are
desktop parts, where a digitizer is rare. Inventing a plausible 12% for the
integrated rows is exactly the guess this codebase keeps having to undo -
the speech-synthesis voices carry the same note for the same reason.
What the machinery buys today is that the value is a SAMPLED PERSONA FIELD
living in invisible_core, not a literal in C++ and not a module constant.
A touchscreen persona (a Surface, a 2-in-1) becomes an edit to this file:
no browser rebuild, no Python change, and the three surfaces a page can
read the touch story from - navigator.maxTouchPoints, typeof window.Touch,
matchMedia('(any-pointer: coarse)') - all follow from this one number,
because prefs.py derives all three from it.
Measured to enable it: 10 is the count a Windows touch digitizer reports.
Do not put 1 here; 1 is what a pen-only or emulated device reports and it
reads as a phone or a devtools emulation to anything that checks.
The draw uses its OWN random stream, named from the seed, NOT the network's
shared rng - see derive_max_touch_points in _sampler.py. A node inside the
network would consume a draw and remap every value sampled after it.
